title: Azure / PostgreSQL flexible server / Overview
description: Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server (microsoft.dbforpostgresql/flexibleservers): Resource Graph inventory, availability, CPU, memory, storage, connections, disk I/O, network, replication, autovacuum, PgBouncer and enhanced metrics. Based on Grafana's bundled 'Azure / Azure PostgreSQL / Flexible Server Monitoring' dashboard (Grafana v12.4, AGPL-3.0). Managed by Terraform (azure-managed-grafana): edit dashboards/postgresql/postgresql-overview.json, not the dashboard in the UI. Changes made in Grafana are overwritten on the next apply.

panels.title: Troubleshooting - $resource
panels.description: Start here when something looks wrong: is the resource running, has an alert fired, what changed? Resource Graph data; it lags a few minutes behind Azure. Grafana's identity needs read access (Monitoring Reader) on the resource.

panels.title: State
panels.description: Current state from Azure Resource Manager. Green: running/ready. Red: stopped, deallocated, failed or disabled. Orange: anything else, e.g. updating or starting.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers' and resourceGroup =~ '$rg' and name =~ '$resource'
| project ['State'] = tostring(properties.state)

panels.title: Open alerts
panels.description: Azure Monitor alerts fired on this resource and not closed (alerts are kept 30 days). History across resources: the bundled Azure / Alert Consumption dashboard.

azureResourceGraph.query:
alertsmanagementresources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.alertsmanagement/alerts'
| extend e = properties.essentials
| where tolower(tostring(e.targetResource)) == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource')
| where tostring(e.monitorCondition) == 'Fired' and tostring(e.alertState) != 'Closed'
| summarize ['Open alerts'] = count()

panels.title: Changes (time range)
panels.description: Resource Manager changes to this resource and its child resources in the time range (Resource Graph change history, kept 14 days). Details on the right.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| summarize Changes = count()

panels.title: What changed
panels.description: Latest Resource Manager changes in the time range: who changed what, with which operation, and which properties. A change just before a problem started is the first suspect.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resourcechanges
| extend target = tolower(tostring(properties.targetResourceId))
| where (target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource') or target startswith strcat(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource'), '/'))
| where todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp) between ($__timeFrom() .. $__timeTo())
| project Time = todatetime(properties.changeAttributes.timestamp),
          Change = tostring(properties.changeType),
          Resource = iff(target == tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource'), '(this resource)', substring(target, strlen(tolower('/subscriptions/$sub/resourceGroups/$rg/providers/Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers/$resource')) + 1)),
          ['Changed by'] = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.changedBy),
          Operation = tostring(properties.changeAttributes.operation),
          Properties = strcat_array(bag_keys(properties.changes), ', ')
| order by Time desc
| take 50

options.content:
# Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server - Monitoring Dashboard
#### - Each metric is emitted at a 1-minute interval and has up to 93 days of history.
#### - For a complete list of metrics, refer to [Azure PostgreSQL Monitoring Metrics](https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/postgresql/monitor/concepts-monitoring)

panels.title: PostgreSQL flexible servers in the subscription
panels.description: Azure Resource Graph: every Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers resource in $sub. StorageGB is the provisioned storage (the limit behind Storage percent). Click a server name to show its metrics below.

azureResourceGraph.query:
resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.dbforpostgresql/flexibleservers'
| project Server = name,
          ResourceGroup = resourceGroup,
          Location = location,
          SKU = tostring(sku.name),
          Tier = tostring(sku.tier),
          Version = tostring(properties.version),
          HAMode = tostring(properties.highAvailability.mode),
          HAState = tostring(properties.highAvailability.state),
          ReplicationRole = tostring(properties.replicationRole),
          StorageGB = toint(properties.storage.storageSizeGB),
          State = tostring(properties.state)
| order by ResourceGroup asc, Server asc

options.content: #### **NOTE**: While metrics are stored for 93 days, you can only query (in the Metrics tile) for a maximum of 30 days worth of data on any single chart. If you see a blank chart or your chart displays only part of metric data, verify that the difference between start and end dates in the time picker doesn't exceed the 30-day interval. After you've selected a 30-day interval, you can pan the chart to view the full retention window.

options.content: #### **NOTE**: PgBouncer metrics are emitted at a 1-minute interval. For PgBouncer metrics to work, both the server parameters `pgbouncer.enabled` and `metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics` must be enabled. Not available on the Burstable tier.

panels.description: Total number of connection pools. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Number of connection pools

panels.description: Connections from clients that are associated with an Azure Database for PostgreSQL connection. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Active client connections

panels.description: Connections to Azure Database for PostgreSQL that are in use by a client connection. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Active server connections

panels.description: Current number of pooled connections. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Total pooled connections

panels.description: Connections from clients that are waiting for an Azure Database for PostgreSQL connection to service them. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Waiting client connections

panels.description: Connections to Azure Database for PostgreSQL that are idle and ready to service a new client connection. PgBouncer metric: requires the server parameters pgbouncer.enabled = true and metrics.pgbouncer_diagnostics = ON. Not available on the Burstable tier.
panels.title: Idle server connections

options.content: #### **NOTE**: Enhanced metrics are emitted at a 1-minute interval. To enable these metrics, set the server parameter `metrics.collector_database_activity` to ON.

panels.description: Number of times disk blocks were found already in the buffer cache, so that a read wasn't necessary. Enhanced metric: requires the server parameter metrics.collector_database_activity = ON (dynamic, no restart). Empty otherwise.

panels.title: Disk Blocks Read
Deadlocks by Database

panels.title: Oldest xmin Age
panels.description: Transactions since the oldest xmin. A steadily growing value means a long-running transaction or a replication slot is holding back vacuum. Enhanced metric: requires the server parameter metrics.collector_database_activity = ON (dynamic, no restart). Empty otherwise.

panels.title: Backends by Database
panels.description: Number of backends connected to each database. Enhanced metric: requires the server parameter metrics.collector_database_activity = ON (dynamic, no restart). Empty otherwise.
Indicates if the database is up or not in the last 30 days
panels.title: Database availability (Last 30 days)

panels.description: Amount of backup storage used. This metric represents the sum of storage that's consumed by all the full backups, differential backups, and log backups that are retained based on the backup retention period that's set for the server. The frequency of the backups is service managed. For geo-redundant storage, backup storage usage is twice the usage for locally redundant storage
